genericProblem: A historical deferred-L2 registry can be read as a permanent exemption after Dexter changes a delivery unit's acceptance scope, allowing unit/static proof to be mistaken for completed browser business evidence.

counterexamples.reason: A test file already exists but is not itself enough: each phase obligation requires a non-empty real browser case through a managed run with business and cleanup evidence.
A Playwright configuration without an injected managed base URL cannot establish a completed L2 run.

findings.finding: The old registry deferred all currently named platform and operations L2 targets to RM2, while the current Dexter instruction explicitly requires P6-2 and P6-3 to complete the L2 tests within their business scopes.
P6-2's prior final-review disposition and PASS package-exit draft depended on the historical defer, so neither can remain a valid closure after the scope correction.

preventionDispositions.reason: The exact surface and test denominators are package-specific and require real managed browser evidence rather than a broad future-phase label.
A material Dexter scope correction reopens any finding disposition and package exit that relied on superseded scope.
